output.headline: Advent offers a fund of about $25 billion and five National deals, but a thin Health IT record makes it a secondary call.
output.differentiator: Advent has done more deals in the target's National region than any other buyer on the priority list (5), and its return at the ask clears the 20% hurdle.
output.why_them: Deep-pocketed sponsor with National reach; Health IT record thin

acquirer_overview.title: A large-fund sponsor with a broad, mostly non-Health IT record
points: 18 deals from 2016 to 2024, 15 closed (83%), and 17 of 18 were control deals [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share].
Home sub-sector is Behavioral Health; 17 of 18 deals were outside Health IT, with Dental, Health Insurance and Revenue Cycle at 3 each [B:buyer, T:record, K:by_sub_sector].
Advent Global Private Equity X, about $25 billion (2022 vintage), gives it capacity for a $300M target [P:1].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Credible on region and size, weak on sub-sector focus
points: Margin Improvement drove 7 of 18 deals, and the target's 25.0% margin suits that playbook [M:margin_improvement, X:target].
Past buying in this or a neighbouring region is a modest factor for; its low share of deals in the target's sub-sector is a slight factor against [S:geo_fit, S:sector_share].
Only 1 of 18 deals was Health IT, and Advent has no open platform, so the target would be a new bet, not an add-on [A:angles].

precedent_activity.title: One Health IT precedent, withdrawn; neighbouring deals show appetite at scale
points: Cascade Health Informatics (Health IT, $125M, Bolt-on, 2018) was priced at 22.6x but withdrawn [D:MA-2018-0206].
Vantage Therapeutics ($315M, SPAC Merger, 2021, National) closed at 19.5x, close to the target's $300M size [D:MA-2021-0203].
Star Practice Management ($106M, Recapitalization, 2022) closed at 20.3x; 4 of 18 deals sit in the $150M-$600M size band [D:MA-2022-0419, K:size_band].

valuation_context.title: Median anchor of 21.4x is affordable, though above Advent's usual price
points: 13 same-sub-sector comparables show 19.4x at the 25th percentile, 21.4x median and 23.3x at the 75th [V:comps].
The 50th percentile is defensible: the 25.0% margin beats the comparables' 22.2% median but is not in their top quarter [V:comps].
Advent's own median paid is 15.5x, below the comparables' median, so it must stretch beyond its habit [T:record, V:comps].
At 5.0x leverage and an equity cheque of $239M, IRR at the ask is 25.3% against a 20% target; maximum price is $356M [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Size and focus stretch
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $124M is under half the $300M EV, and Health IT is 1 of 18 deals [T:record].
risk_flags.mitigant: Its biggest deal was $5,537M, and 4 of 18 deals sit in the comparable size band [T:record, K:size_band].
risk_flags.reality: Size is feasible, but this would be a new sub-sector bet with no open platform [A:angles].

risk_flags.title: Pricing habit below the market
risk_flags.concern: Advent's median paid of 15.5x trails the comparables' 21.4x median [T:record, V:comps].
risk_flags.mitigant: It paid 20.3x for Star Practice Management and 19.5x for Vantage Therapeutics [D:MA-2022-0419, D:MA-2021-0203].
risk_flags.reality: A bid near the median is possible, but the one Health IT deal at 22.6x was withdrawn [D:MA-2018-0206].

risk_flags.title: Crowded process
risk_flags.concern: Advent ranks 10th of 10 on the priority list, 13th overall, at a 3.5% likelihood [R:rank].
risk_flags.mitigant: Past buying in this or a neighbouring region is a modest factor in its favour [S:geo_fit].
risk_flags.reality: Buyers with deeper Health IT records will likely lead the process [R:rank].

conviction.rationale: Only 1 deal sits in the target's own sub-sector, there is no open platform, and the $124M median deal is under half the $300M EV, so the case rests on capacity and return rather than fit [C:conviction, T:record].
